sections.title: Another verb like tetszik
sections.content: ízlik ("to taste good, to be to someone's liking") is built the same way as tetszik, which you've already used to react to things (Igen, tetszik! "Yes, I like it!") without stopping to ask why. The food itself is the grammatical subject, and the person it tastes good to — when you name them at all — goes in the dative you already know: nekem ízlik a leves is literally "to me, the soup is pleasing." Most of the time, exactly like tetszik, the dative pronoun is simply dropped when it's obvious who you mean.

items.english: The soup tastes really good (to me)!

sections.content: kedvenc doesn't change form as an adjective (kedvenc ételem, "my favourite food"), but it can also stand alone as a noun with a possessive ending — a kedvencem, "my favourite [one]" — exactly the way you'd use enyém for "mine."
